obj.tagih: Catat tagihan di amplop, lalu cek dapur dan dompet
obj.kerja: Cari kerja: proyek bangunan, lalu pasar
obj.konstruksi: Datang ke proyek, tanya pekerjaan ke mandor
obj.panggil: Ponsel berdering di rumah. Balik dan jawab telepon pinjol
obj.pulang: Selesaikan urusan pagi, lalu keluar rumah

kasur.1: Jam dinding menunjuk tujuh lewat lima. Sinar pagi masuk lewat celah jendela.
kasur.2: Hari baru. Semoga hari ini beda.
kasur.3: Kaki menyentuh lantai. Dingin. Tapi harus bangun.

dapur.1: Dapur hanya berisi kompor mati dan satu panci kosong.
dapur.2: Beras tinggal segenggam. Nanti beli di pasar.

amplop.1: Di meja makan ada tumpukan amplop. Semua belum dibuka.
amplop.2: Tagihan, tagihan, lagi. Tanggal jatuh temponya sudah lewat semua.
amplop.3: Kutulis lagi di catatan ponsel. Angkanya tidak pernah berubah.

dompet.1: Dompet kulit itu tipis. Isinya bisa dihitung pakai satu tangan.
dompet.2: Delapan puluh lima ribu. Cukup buat sekali makan. Tidak cukup buat apa pun.

foto.1: Foto keluarga di dinding: empat orang berdiri di depan rumah lama.
foto.2: Cat di bingkai sudah mengelupas. Wajah di dalamnya belum berubah.

obeng.1: Di sisa perkakas dapur ada obeng bergagang oranye. Gagangnya masih terasa hangat.
obeng.2: Kotak sekring di dinding ruang tengah. Tutupnya dipegang sekrup. Ini pasti pas.

terkunci.1: Kotak sekring tertutup rapat. Empat sekrup menatapmu dari balik pelat logam.
terkunci.2: Butuh obeng. Di dapur tadi ada perkakas. Siapa tahu ada yang cocok.

buka.1: Sekrup berputar satu per satu. Tutup pelat terlepas dengan bunyi letih.
buka.2: Di baliknya, menggantung di antara kabel, ada kunci kecil bertali karet. Kunci laci.

sudah.1: Kotak sekring sudah terbuka. Isinya tinggal kabel yang diam.

terkunci.1: Laci ruang tengah tidak mau membuka. Ada empat angka di pelat kuncinya.
terkunci.2: Kunci kecil Ibu... dia selalu menyimpannya di kotak sekring, katanya biar tidak hilang.

kosong.1: Laci sudah terbuka dan kosong. Senter yang tadi di dalamnya kini di tasmu.

p1.title: Laci Ruang Tengah
p1.desc: Kunci sudah terpasang, tapi tutupnya dijaga empat angka. Senter di dalam menunggu.
p1.hint1: Jam dinding di rumah ini berhenti. Angka yang ditunjuknya sempat kau baca saat bangun.
p1.hint2: Tujuh lewat lima. Empat angka tanpa titik.

proyek.1: Di proyek bangunan, mandor sedang mengecek tumpukan semen.
proyek.2: Maaf, Mas. Lagi gak buka lowongan. Bulan depan coba lagi lah.
proyek.4: Tangan Dimas kosong saat berbalik ke jalan.

pasar.1: Pedagang nasi bungkus masih buka. Bau santan naik ke hidung.
pasar.cnasi: Beli nasi bungkus, lima belas ribu

nasi.1: Ambil satu. Malam nanti masih harus makan.

hemat.1: Tahan dulu. Uang ini buat jaga-jaga.

kerja.1: Sambil di pasar, Dimas menawarkan diri mengangkut barang.
kerja.2: Anak si Fulan udah bantu saya, Mas. Sori ya.

panggilan.1: Bapak Dimas, ini terkait tunggakan pembayaran yang sudah lewat empat belas hari. Kami harap Bapak menunjukkan itikad baik.
panggilan.2: Telepon bergetar di tangan. Jari Dimas menggantung di atas layar.
panggilan.3: Telepon itu tidak akan berhenti sendiri.

angkat.1: Pak, saya masih cari kerja. Bulan ini pasti saya bayar.
angkat.2: Kami tunggu sampai akhir bulan, Bapak.

tolak.1: Telepon dipatikan sebelum penagih selesai bicara.

diam.1: Telepon berdering sampai berhenti sendiri. Ruangan terasa lebih sepi.

akhir.1: Dimas duduk di lantai, menyandar ke dinding.
akhir.2: Angka-angka itu tidak berubah. Besok harus ada yang berubah.

halt.1: Nanti dulu. Lihat isi rumah dulu.
halt.2: Ke proyek dulu. Pagi-pagi biasanya mandor ada di sana.
halt.3: Belum ke pasar. Mampir dulu, siapa tahu ada yang butuh tangan.

semen.1: Semen ditumpuk rapi di sudut. Nama pabriknya sudah pudar kena hujan.

perancah.1: Perancah bambu setinggi dua lantai. Papan pijakannya goyang ketika disentuh.
perancah.2: Kalau jatuh dari sini, tidak ada yang tahu sampai sore.

spanduk.1: Spanduk proyek: DIBUKA KERJA HARIAN. Di sudut kiri ada catatan tulisan tangan.

lapak.1: Sayuran tertata rapi per jenis. Harga ditulis di papan tulis kecil.

keranjang.1: Keranjang anyaman penuh kulit bawang. Entah berapa kali dipindah hari ini.

spanduk_pasar.1: Papan selamat datang di pintu pasar. Catnya mengelupas di beberapa huruf.

keluar.1: Pagi sudah tinggi. Pintu depan menunggu.

proyek.1: Pintu ditutup. Jalan kampung menuju proyek terasa panas walau matahari baru naik.

pasar.1: Pintu ditutup. Pasar sudah ramai ketika kaki menyentuh tanah lapang.

pergi.1: Kunci pintunya. Semoga sore nanti ada kabar baik.

tunggu.1: Belum. Masih ada yang harus dibereskan dulu.

jalan.1: Pintu keluar proyek. Dari sini jalan bercabang: ke pasar atau balik ke rumah.

pasar.1: Kaki memutar melewati tumpukan batu. Bau semen masih menempel di baju.

rumah.1: Belum ada kabar. Pulang dulu, siapa tahu ada yang meninggalkan pesan.

tunggu.1: Di bawah bayang perancah, debu proyek berputar di udara pagi.

jalan_pasar.1: Keluar pasar. Jalan setapak kembali ke rumah menyeberangi lapang.

rumah.1: Langkah diputar ke rumah. Ponsel masih di meja. Entah siapa yang menelepon tadi.

tunggu.1: Keranjang ditata ulang. Penjual sibuk dengan urusannya sendiri.

obj.rumah: Check the house: kitchen, envelopes, wallet
obj.tagih: Note the bills in the envelopes, then check kitchen and wallet
obj.kerja: Look for work: building site, then the market
obj.konstruksi: Go to the site and ask the foreman for work
obj.ke_pasar: Offer your services at the market
obj.panggil: The phone is ringing at home. Go back and answer the loan call
obj.pulang: Finish the morning, then leave the house

kasur.1: The wall clock reads five past seven. Morning light slips through the window gap.
kasur.2: A new day. I hope today is different.
kasur.3: My feet touch the floor. Cold. But I have to get up.

dapur.1: The kitchen holds nothing but a dead stove and one empty pot.
dapur.2: Only a handful of rice left. I will buy some at the market later.

amplop.1: A stack of envelopes sits on the table. None of them are open.
amplop.2: Bills, bills, again. Every due date has already passed.
amplop.3: I write them into my phone notes again. The numbers never change.

dompet.1: The leather wallet is thin. I can count what is inside with one hand.
dompet.2: Eighty five thousand. Enough for one meal. Not enough for anything.

a.1: Same result. The numbers do not change.

b.1: Never mind. Money will come somehow.

akhir.1: Okay. Time to go. Work first.

foto.1: A family photo on the wall: four people standing in front of the old house.
foto.2: The paint on the frame has peeled. The faces inside have not changed.

obeng.1: Among the leftover kitchen tools lies a screwdriver with an orange handle. It still feels warm.
obeng.2: The fuse box on the living room wall. Its cover is held by screws. This must fit.
obeng.sudah: The screwdriver is already in your bag.

terkunci.1: The fuse box is shut tight. Four screws stare at you from behind the metal plate.
terkunci.2: You need a screwdriver. There were tools in the kitchen. Maybe one fits.

buka.1: The screws turn one by one. The plate comes loose with a tired click.
buka.2: Behind it, hanging between the wires, is a small key on a rubber band. A drawer key.

sudah.1: The fuse box is already open. Only the silent wires remain inside.

terkunci.1: The living room drawer won't budge. Four numbers sit on its lock plate.
terkunci.2: Mother's little key... she always kept it in the fuse box, she said, so it wouldn't get lost.

kosong.1: The drawer is open and empty. The flashlight that was inside is now in your bag.

p1.title: Living Room Drawer
p1.desc: The key is in, but four numbers guard the lock. The flashlight inside is waiting.
p1.hint1: The wall clock in this house has stopped. You read its numbers when you woke up.
p1.hint2: Five past seven. Four digits without a dot.

proyek.1: At the building site, the foreman is checking stacks of cement.
proyek.2: Sorry, Mas. We are not taking anyone right now. Try again next month.
proyek.4: Dimas's hands are empty when he turns back to the road.

pasar.1: The rice wrap seller is still open. The smell of coconut milk reaches his nose.
pasar.cnasi: Buy a rice wrap, fifteen thousand

nasi.1: Take one. I still have to eat tonight.

hemat.1: Hold on. This money is for emergencies.

kerja.1: While at the market, Dimas offers to carry goods.
kerja.2: Fulan's boy already helps me, Mas. Sorry.
kerja.3: That is fine, sir. Thanks for the information.
kerja.4: He walks home with empty hands.

panggilan.1: Mr Dimas, this concerns a payment overdue by fourteen days. We hope you show good faith.
panggilan.2: The phone buzzes in his hand. Dimas's finger hovers over the screen.
panggilan.3: The call will not stop on its own.

angkat.1: Sir, I am still looking for work. I will pay this month, I promise.
angkat.2: We will wait until the end of the month, sir.

tolak.1: The call is cut before the collector finishes speaking.

diam.1: The phone rings until it stops by itself. The room feels emptier.

akhir.1: Dimas sits on the floor, leaning against the wall.
akhir.2: The numbers do not change. Tomorrow something has to change.

halt.1: Later. Let me see what is in the house first.
halt.2: To the site first. The foreman is usually there early.
halt.3: Not the market yet. A stop first, in case someone needs hands.

semen.1: Cement bags are stacked neatly in the corner, the mill's name faded by rain.

perancah.1: Bamboo scaffolding two storeys high. The planks wobble when touched.
perancah.2: If someone falls from here, nobody would know until evening.

spanduk.1: Site banner: DAILY WORKERS WANTED. There is a handwritten note in the left corner.

lapak.1: Vegetables sorted neatly by type. Prices are written on a small chalkboard.

keranjang.1: Woven baskets full of onion skins. Who knows how many times they moved today.

spanduk_pasar.1: A welcome board at the market gate. The paint is peeling off some letters.

keluar.1: The morning is high now. The front door waits.

proyek.1: The door closes. The path to the site already feels hot, though the sun has just risen.

pasar.1: The door closes. The market is already busy when his feet touch the open ground.

pergi.1: Lock the door. I hope there is good news by evening.

tunggu.1: Not yet. There is still something to finish first.

jalan.1: The way out of the site. From here the road forks: to the market, or back home.

pasar.1: He cuts past the brick stacks. Cement dust still clings to his shirt.

rumah.1: No news yet. Head home first, maybe someone left a message.

tunggu.1: Under the scaffold's shadow, site dust spins in the morning air.

jalan_pasar.1: Out of the market. The path home crosses the field.

rumah.1: He turns for home. The phone is still on the table, who could be calling?

tunggu.1: The woven baskets are stacked again. The sellers are busy with their own affairs.
